newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE STOCKS UP ON BARGAIN HUNTING, IGNORE DLR.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE STOCKS UP ON BARGAIN HUNTING, IGNORE DLR.

text.p: Singapore shares rallied in early trade on Tuesday as dealers picked up cheap industrial stocks and shrugged off a sharp fall in the Singapore dollar.
By 0140 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) tracking blue chips was 11.33 points higher at 1,905.19.
On Monday, it dipped to four-year lows and ended 2.58 percent, or 50.06 points, down at 1,893.86.
Dealers said there was a general perception that Singapore stocks were inexpensive after their recent falls but many investors were still worried it might not yet be time to buy.
"Singapore is suffering from the turbulence in other markets like Thailand," said one local dealer. "But in the longer-term, this is an opportunity to buy."
Dealers said a dip in the value of the Singapore dollar, which fell to around 1.5050 to the U.S. dollar from around 1.4850/70 early on Tuesday, had not affected the stock market.
The Singapore currency fell after comments by a finance official that dealers interpreted as leaving open the possibility of further exchange rate falls.

Top of the early stock market volume was venture capital firm Hotung Investment, which rose two cents to US$0.53 on its second day of trading. Almost half of the 20 million shares traded in Hotung were crossed off the market.
